Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below: 

• Yes, we can invoice to Aurelia Health Services LLC (we just need the remit-to and W-9 or equivalent).
• We prefer a single invoice per billing period (monthly) where possible — we can support consolidated invoicing if the paying entity will accept responsibility for the entire invoice and provide a PO referencing the consolidated account.
• Withholding: we generally invoice gross; any withholding that Aurelia applies is your responsibility. If you require Redwood to gross-up, we need to capture that in the Order Form appendix and reflect it in the pricing table.

Detailed notes: 
1) Invoicing entity: To invoice to the LLC instead of the Inc. please confirm legal name, remit-to address, and provide a U.S. taxpayer ID / W-9. Once we have that, Finance will set up the remit-to and route invoices accordingly.

2) Consolidated invoice option: We can issue one consolidated invoice if Aurelia confirms in writing that "Aurelia Health Services LLC" will accept payment liability for the entire consolidated amount. If you need separate legal entity invoices (for entity-level expense accounting), we can produce per-entity invoices but will need entity-level billing contacts and separate POs. Note this may affect how credits/true-ups are handled against minimum commits.

3) Tax handling and gross-up: For the Order Form to absorb gross-up we need a line item in the payment section: "Seller shall gross-up amounts to account for any withholding taxes imposed on payments" and a clause in the pricing appendix to reflect adjusted unit rates. That will require approval from Redwood Legal (cc'ing Kim).

I attached a simple diagram of the flow we typically use (see invoice_flow_diagram.png). Happy to run a quick 15-min call to align with your AP.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Emily's questions plus my suggested language for the Order Form appendix. Key points: 

1) Invoicing entity / remit-to: Redwood can invoice to the LLC if the customer supplies a completed W-9 and the remit-to address. Add the following conditions to the Order Form: "Customer shall provide valid tax documentation for the invoice recipient. Seller may decline electronic invoice routing changes until documentation is verified."

2) Consolidated invoicing: Proposed clause: "Customer may request consolidated invoicing across related entities provided an Authorized Payor form is executed designating the entity that will accept payment liability. Consolidated invoicing does not alter the allocation of minimum commit liability across the entities unless otherwise agreed in writing." This protects Redwood on minimum commit allocation.

3) Withholding / gross-up: Proposed optional appendix language: "If Customer requires Seller to gross-up payments to offset withholding taxes, Customer shall (i) notify Seller at least 30 days prior to the first payment subject to withholding, (ii) provide documentation of the withholding rate, and (iii) reimburse Seller for any administrative costs associated with tax gross-up. Gross-up will require pricing adjustment and sign-off by Seller's finance team."

I flagged the gross-up as higher risk and recommended holding pricing clarifications to avoid open-ended liabilities. Also recommended a specific acceptance step: request AP contact, remit-to, and W-9 be provided prior to go-live.

If agreeable, I'll produce a tracked redline of the Order Form appendix and the MSA payment schedule. I attached a short redline doc (Aurelia_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx).

—Kimberly Park
